prompt: Solve the inequality $-3x > 12$. Write your answer like "x < -4".
hint: To isolate $x$ you must divide by a negative number. Remember the special rule for inequalities when you do that.

hints.text: To isolate $x$ you must divide by a negative number. Remember the special rule for inequalities when you do that.
Divide both sides by $-3$ and reverse the sign, so $>$ becomes $<$. Then work out $12 \div (-3)$.
$12 \div (-3) = -4$ and the sign flips, so the solution set is $x < -4$.

explanation: Divide both sides by $-3$ to get $x$ alone, and flip the inequality sign: $x < -4$.
The flip is needed because multiplying or dividing by a negative reverses the order of numbers on the number line.
Check with a value below $-4$: $x = -5$ gives $-3(-5) = 15$, and $15 > 12$ is true, so $x < -4$.

alternativeExplanations.title: See why the flip is real
steps: Multiply both sides by $-1$: you get $-2$ and $-6$, and now $-2 > -6$.
Negatives reverse the order on the number line, so the sign MUST flip.
